problem: Existing attacks on embodied navigation are impractical (perturbing the agent's camera view, or re-texturing whole 3D objects) and physical patch attacks for detection fail to be both effective across diverse viewpoints and visually natural on objects.
motivation: Embodied navigation agents are used in safety-critical settings, yet their perception models (e.g. Mask R-CNN) are vulnerable to adversarial examples. A realistic threat model has attackers who cannot change the victim's model or camera but can modify the physical environment, so a physically realizable and inconspicuous attack is needed.
key_idea: Attach an adversarial patch with learnable RGB texture and learnable opacity to the target object, optimized through a differentiable renderer over object-aware sampled viewpoints, with texture optimized first and opacity second.
insight: Multi-view optimization matters: raising ASR from 74.38 (single view) to 89.26 (20 views). The second-stage opacity optimization raises ASR further to 98.35 while making the patch more natural. Opacity only helps when the texture is already adversarially optimized: with random textures, ASR stays at 15.70-29.75 whatever the opacity, whereas optimized textures reach 90.91 at opacity 0.6.
method: Patch parameterization: a 512x512 RGBA patch, with a 3-channel RGB texture and a single-channel opacity mask, initialized with Gaussian noise and manually positioned on the target object.

Object-aware sampling: cameras are placed on circles of several radii around the target object, with random initialization. Viewpoints are kept only if the detector's confidence is at least tau (0.5), giving a viewpoint distribution V.
Differentiable rendering (Mitsuba 3): first-person images with and without the patch are rendered under specified lighting and viewpoint, then fed to Mask R-CNN.

Attack loss: a weighted sum of Mask R-CNN classification, box regression, RPN classification and RPN localization losses (lambda = [0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1]), maximized with PGD for 100 iterations at step size 1 across the views.

Two-stage opacity optimization: stage 1 optimizes the texture with constant opacity; stage 2 optimizes only the opacity mask on the fixed texture, to avoid conflicting gradients and reduce human visibility.
Evaluation in ObjectNav: white-box attack on the PEANUT modular agent (Mask R-CNN) in Habitat/HM3D, plus a multi-view detection ASR test on 100 unseen viewpoints.

setting.backbone: PEANUT modular ObjectNav agent with Mask R-CNN segmentation (attacked, frozen); the adversarial patch is optimized
setting.training_data: No model training; the patch is optimized per target object in one HM3D validation scene (20 viewpoints for optimization)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (the segmentation model input; PEANUT also uses depth)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions from the PEANUT modular agent (map-based goal selection and planning)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D scenes) with Mitsuba 3 for differentiable rendering of patches
setting.privileged: white-box access to the detector's gradients; patch manually placed on the target object; optimization scenes from the validation set

numbers.eval_set_note: per target category, one randomly selected HM3D val scene containing the object, 100 episodes with random initial positions; average over 6 categories (tv monitor, plant, bed, chair, sofa, toilet)
numbers.extra: Attack paper: lower SR/SPL and higher DTS are better for the attacker. Baseline No Attack average: SR 94.85, SPL 51.87, DTS 0.39; Camouflage: SR 84.44, SPL 45.08, DTS 0.56.

numbers.eval_set_note: 120 viewpoints around a television monitor: 20 for optimization, 100 unseen for testing
numbers.extra: No Attack 19.01; Camouflage 85.12; Ours texture only 89.26
numbers.evidence: Table 2: Ours Patch (Multi-view Optimized Texture & Opacity) 98.35

numbers_note: Attack paper: metrics measure the drop in navigation performance, not navigation quality. Per-category results are in Table 1 but only the average is listed here.
results: The patch lowers average ObjectNav SR from 94.85 to 72.46 (a 22.39-point drop) and SPL from 51.87 to 30.99, beating the 3D camouflage baseline (SR 84.44). On multi-view detection it reaches 98.35% ASR versus 85.12% for camouflage.
limitations: Simulation only; there are no real-world physical experiments, and human perceptibility is not evaluated.
Cross-renderer transferability is weak (habitat-sim does not support transparent materials), and the attack is white-box and manually placed.
Evaluated on one scene per category with 100 episodes, on only one modular agent (PEANUT); the SR drop varies widely (0 for bed, 40 for tv monitor), and camouflage is stronger on plants.
